article_title: Development of Habits Through Apprenticeship in a Community: Conceptual Model of Physics Teacher Preparation
citation: Eugenia Etkina, Bor Gregorcic, and Stamatis Vokos. (2022). Development of Habits Through Apprenticeship in a Community: Conceptual Model of Physics Teacher Preparation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03527
title: DHAC: a conceptual model of teacher preparation centered on habit formation within a community of practice
description: DHAC (Development of Habits through Apprenticeship in a Community) holds that teacher preparation programs must develop desired habits grounded in knowledge, skills, and dispositions nurtured by a community. The authors argue that habits are the missing link between intentional decision-making and actual teaching practice, since real-time classroom demands leave no time for deliberation on every decision. A tree analogy illustrates the model: roots are knowledge, skills, and dispositions lived out by the community; the trunk is habits of mind and practice; the canopy is habits of maintenance enabling professional growth.
requirements: A community of like-minded teachers working toward a shared vision of good teaching, since habits form from the interaction of knowledge, skills, and dispositions within that community
constraints: The model is generic but useful only when furnished with discipline-specific content; the authors note it is instantiated here for physics and that time and further research will show its practical usefulness
target_learning_goals: habits of mind and practice that support reformed physics teaching
examples: The paper uses the tree-environment analogy in which the trunk represents habits of mind and practice that let the teacher stand on their own feet in unpredictable classroom circumstances
key_sources: Eugenia Etkina, Bor Gregorcic, and Stamatis Vokos. (2022). Development of Habits Through Apprenticeship in a Community: Conceptual Model of Physics Teacher Preparation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03527

article_title: Development of Habits Through Apprenticeship in a Community: Conceptual Model of Physics Teacher Preparation
citation: Eugenia Etkina, Bor Gregorcic, and Stamatis Vokos. (2022). Development of Habits Through Apprenticeship in a Community: Conceptual Model of Physics Teacher Preparation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03527
title: Definitions of knowledge, skills, and dispositions as distinct inputs to habit formation in the DHAC model
description: The model distinguishes three inputs to habit formation. Knowledge spans conceptual and quantitative understanding of physics, including the ability to explain phenomena in simple words and representations non-physicists understand. A skill is defined as a pre-compiled procedure deployed automatically, broken into mental, technical, and emotional skills. A disposition is defined as a strong, often subconscious belief or attitude related to some aspect of teaching, illustrated by how beliefs about who can learn physics change assessment practices. Skills are treated separately from habits because being skilled in something does not necessarily mean doing it habitually.
requirements: Dispositions determine what knowledge and skills PSTs choose to appropriate during the program, so dispositions are treated first
constraints: The authors seek a minimal set of inputs, all founded on their stated assumptions or serving the grand unifying theme
target_learning_goals: foundational knowledge, skills, and dispositions undergirding teaching habits
examples: The drinking-water example illustrates the skill-habit distinction: everyone is skilled in drinking water but not everyone habitually drinks the requisite number of glasses a day
key_sources: Eugenia Etkina, Bor Gregorcic, and Stamatis Vokos. (2022). Development of Habits Through Apprenticeship in a Community: Conceptual Model of Physics Teacher Preparation. https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.03527
